newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen Airways pilots on strike for better pay.
newsitem.headline: Yemen Airways pilots on strike for better pay.

text.p: Pilots, co-pilots and engineers at Yemen Airways on Thursday began an open-ended strike to demand better pay, disrupting air traffic to and from the Arab state, an airline official said.
"They resumed their partial strike as of today and have left it open until their demands are met," an airline official told Reuters.

"They decided that the strike would go on from 2 p.m. (1100 GMT) to 8 a.m. (0500 GMT) every day after the deadline set by the transport minister to settle their demands expired without him finding a solution to their problems," he said.
"During the strike period, no Yemen Airways flight will take off or land, whether on an internal or on a foreign trip".
The 160 strikers held a one-day partial protest on May 15, grounding all of the airline's planes and threatened to hold more protests if the company's board of directors failed to heed their demands.
The strike did not affect flights by other airlines servicing Yemen, officials said.

Yemen Airways pays its pilots and co-pilots between 35,000 rials ($280) and 75,000 rials a month, depending on the duration of service with the company, employees said. Some of the flight staff have joined other regional carriers who offer better salaries.
The Sanaa-based airline was formed last year by the merger of Yemenia Airways and Al-Yemda -- the carriers of the former North Yemen and South Yemen which united in 1990.
With a fleet of 13 aircraft -- four Boeing 727s, one Boeing 707, three Boeing 737, three de Havilland Dash-7s and two Airbus A 310s -- the airline flies to 23 destinations in Asia, Africa and Europe.
